BoardGroupInfo.description: A physical board and the targets living inside it.
BoardGroupInfo.title: BoardGroupInfo

BoardRuntimeInfo.description:
Per-board runtime + synthesised in-use status.

The first four fields (``name``, ``bound_busids``, ``attached_ports``,
``remote_host``) are the original runtime-only shape from
pre-status-synthesis callers — preserved so JSON consumers that read
only these keys keep working. The remaining fields come from
:func:`fpgahub.status.compute_status` and default to idle values so
tests that construct a ``BoardRuntimeInfo`` by hand don't need to
fill them.
BoardRuntimeInfo.title: BoardRuntimeInfo

ChassisLeaseCancelRequest.description:
Body for ``DELETE /boards/{name}/queue`` and
``DELETE /targets/{name}/queue``.

A4: this used to identify the waiter *by holder string*, and every
web user's holder was the hub's hostname — so any write-role user
could cancel any other's wait. A caller cancels their own wait and
needs to name nobody; an admin may name a ``holder`` to cancel
somebody else's, and only an admin's is honoured.
ChassisLeaseCancelRequest.title: ChassisLeaseCancelRequest

ChassisLeaseHistoryResponse.description:
Lease audit-log events merged across every member of a chassis,
sorted by timestamp. Each event keeps its ``board`` field so consumers
can attribute rows back to a specific member.
ChassisLeaseHistoryResponse.title: ChassisLeaseHistoryResponse

LeaseAcquireRequest.description:
Body for every lease acquire.

Carries *what* is being asked for, never *who* is asking. A3: the
caller is resolved once, from the transport, into a
:class:`~fpgahub.api.principal.Principal`, and the lease records
``principal.holder`` / ``principal.name``.

``holder``, ``user`` and ``unix_user`` are no longer fields.
Pydantic ignores unknown keys, so an older CLI that still sends them
keeps working for one release; a validator logs a deprecation the
first time each is seen, rather than failing a caller mid-phase.
``source_ip`` stays, but the handler fills it from the request —
the ethernet gate opens a firewall pinhole to that address, which is
precisely the thing a caller must not be able to choose.
LeaseAcquireRequest.title: LeaseAcquireRequest

LeaseEventRecord.description: One entry from the lease-event audit log's tail buffer.
LeaseEventRecord.title: LeaseEventRecord

LeaseHeartbeatRequest.description:
The token proves the lease; the principal proves the caller.

``holder`` is gone for the same reason as on
:class:`LeaseAcquireRequest` — it is matched against
``principal.holder``, so sending it could only ever disagree.
LeaseHeartbeatRequest.title: LeaseHeartbeatRequest

LeaseReleaseRequest.description:
See :class:`LeaseHeartbeatRequest`. A4: release used to take a
holder string, which is how a web user could release somebody
else's board.
LeaseReleaseRequest.title: LeaseReleaseRequest

LeaseTier.description:
Two-tier lease priority.

``INTERACTIVE`` (default — every pre-tier caller) preempts ``BACKGROUND``.
A background holder is revoked when an interactive caller arrives;
background callers always queue behind interactive ones. See
``docs/PROPOSAL_BACKGROUND_TIER.md`` for the full rationale.
LeaseTier.title: LeaseTier

LeaseWaitGrantedResponse.description:
Successful response from ``GET /boards|targets/{id}/lease/wait``.

Returned when the caller's token holds the chassis (or every
member of it) at the moment of return. Carries the per-member
lease snapshots so callers don't need a follow-up GET.
LeaseWaitGrantedResponse.title: LeaseWaitGrantedResponse

PrincipalLimits.description: What ``[policy]`` allows this caller, beyond a role.
PrincipalLimits.title: PrincipalLimits

WhoAmIResponse.description:
``GET /whoami`` — the principal this request resolved to.

The point of the route is that "what am I allowed to do, and as whom
is it recorded" is answerable *before* trying an action and being
refused. ``holder`` is the string a lease will be recorded under, so a
user can tell whether the hub sees them as themselves or as their
workstation.
WhoAmIResponse.title: WhoAmIResponse

delete.description:
Release every chassis member this principal holds under ``token``.

A4: the holder came off the payload, so "release" was really "force
release, unaudited". It is now the caller's own lease or nothing;
taking somebody else's is the admin revoke below.

get.description:
Return the chassis-level lease summary.

The chassis is considered 'held' when every member has a lease
from the same (holder, token). A partially held chassis (some
members free, some held) is reported as held by whoever holds the
majority — operators see a truthful picture but the chassis
acquire endpoint will still refuse cleanly when they try to take it.

Includes ``queue`` (FCFS, 1-indexed) so dashboards can render
"Queue: N waiting" / "You are #M in queue" without a second
round-trip. ``queue_length`` is a convenience scalar.

post.description:
Atomically acquire (or queue) a lease across every member of the chassis.

May return:

- 200 ``granted`` — every member ended up holding a single shared
  token. Release / heartbeat at chassis level uses that token.
- 200 ``queued`` — every held member is held by the *same* other
  holder, so the request was queued FCFS. ``position`` is 1-indexed.
- 409 — heterogeneous third-party holders across members.

get.description:
Lease audit-log events merged across every member of a chassis.

``limit`` applies *per member* — the merged response can therefore
contain up to ``limit * len(members)`` entries. Events are sorted
by timestamp so consumers don't need to interleave themselves.

post.description:
Admin force-release: kick every member's lease on the chassis
regardless of holder/token. Promotes the next FCFS waiter exactly
like a normal release. Admin-only.

The audit trail records ``principal.audit_id`` — ``unix:alice``,
``token:ci-1``, ``session:bob`` — rather than the flat
``"unix-socket-admin"`` every local revoke used to be attributed to.

delete.description:
Remove a queued waiter from a chassis-level FCFS queue.

Idempotent: returns ``{removed: false}`` if no matching waiter is
found. Returns 404 if the chassis itself is unknown so callers can
distinguish "wrong URL" from "your wait already cleared".

get.description:
Server-Sent Events stream of daemon state changes.

Filters (ANDed — all set filters must match):

* ``types``:    comma-separated ``Event.type`` values (e.g.
                ``action.start,action.log,action.end``)
* ``board``:    only events whose ``data.board`` equals the given name
* ``action_id``: only events whose ``data.action_id`` matches
* ``run_id``:   only events whose ``data.run_id`` matches

``board`` + ``action_id`` let a client start streaming before it knows
the ``run_id`` (the dispatch handler is what assigns run_ids). Once
the first ``action.start`` arrives carrying the run_id, the client
can reconnect with a ``run_id`` filter if it wants a tighter view;
in practice the board+action_id pair is unique mid-dispatch thanks to
the per-board mutex.

Return the configured boards organised by physical chassis.

Pairs boards that share a ``chassis`` id (or an auto-derived one
from the ``_ps`` / ``_pl`` suffix convention) so UI / CLI consumers
can render one entry per physical enclosure.

Block until ``token`` holds the board, or ``timeout`` elapses.

Idempotent and safe to call while ``token`` already holds the
board — returns immediately in that case. Designed for the
revoke-with-requeue flow: after a revoke, the original token is
preserved and re-installed on regrant, so a CI script polling
this endpoint sees the same shape on either side of the revoke.

delete.description:
Remove a queued waiter from a target-level FCFS queue.

For a target in a multi-target board the queue lives at the board
level — return 409 ``board_required`` pointing the caller at the
board endpoint so the dashboard / CLI can route the cancel
correctly. A single-target board (board id == target name) hits the
existing per-target ``cancel_wait``.

Stop **every** share on this board.

Which is why it needs more than ``write``: S1 left it gated on the
role alone, so any ``write`` caller could cut the console out from
under the person holding the board (F2). There is no per-share
ownership signal to gate on — the lease is the ownership signal, and
it is the one the dispatchers use, so `fpgahub share stop` still
works for the person who started it.

get.description:
Who the hub thinks you are, and what that lets you do.

Answers for every transport — unix socket, Bearer token, mTLS peer,
web session — because it reports the resolved principal rather than
re-deriving identity per credential. ``read`` is enough to call it:
the reply is about the caller and tells them nothing about anyone
else. ``fpgahub whoami`` is this route.
